title: a prose comment in shellcheck directive position silently disarms the checker for the rest of the script
body:
A comment that BEGINS `# shellcheck ` is directive syntax, so a sentence written there disarms shellcheck for the rest of the script -- silently, in the project that arms shellcheck as a critic.

**Measured by devbin-vc on 2026-09-22, in Intent's own `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, and driven rather than reasoned.** `actionlint .github/workflows/tests.yml` at HEAD, before any edit, reported SC1072 "Expected '=' after directive key" and SC1073 "Couldn't parse this shellcheck directive. Fix to allow more checks", both anchored at the `run:` of the macOS job's "Install dependencies" step. To establish that it predated the edit rather than inferring it from the diff, the file was extracted with `git show HEAD:.github/workflows/tests.yml` into a clean scratch tree and actionlint run there: the same two codes. After rewording so the line no longer begins with the directive token, actionlint reports nothing at all for the file -- **so the re-enabled checks came back clean, and nothing was hiding behind the silence.**

**The mechanism.** A comment beginning `# shellcheck ` is a DIRECTIVE and takes one of six keys: `disable`, `enable`, `source`, `shell`, `external-sources`, `source-path`. The offending line began `# shellcheck IS AN ARMED TOOL FOR THIS PROJECT`, and `IS` is not a key, so the directive is unparseable -- and shellcheck's answer to an unparseable directive is to STOP CHECKING THE REST OF THAT SCRIPT. SC1073's own text says so: "Fix to allow more checks".

**Why this is worth more than its instance.** The sentence was written to emphasise that shellcheck is armed here, and its effect was to disarm it. The general shape, cc's wording: a tool whose own configuration surface accepts prose will read a comment as configuration, and BEING DISARMED IS NOT A STATE IT REPORTS. The failure is a silent loss of checking rather than a red, so nothing distinguishes a script whose checks were skipped from a script that passed them -- which is why it survived in a tracked workflow, in the one project that arms shellcheck as a critic, until an unrelated fleet sweep tripped over it.

**Fixed in this tree already**, at `9d9eb6c52`, by the devbin 0.1.6 sweep that found it. This issue exists for the POPULATION, not the instance.

**The cheap census, not yet run outside devbin and Intent.** `git grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*shellcheck[[:space:]]+'` over a tracked tree, minus the six real keys, names every prose comment sitting in directive position. devbin-cc ran it over devbin's whole tracked tree: devbin is clean, so devbin's ShellCheck leg green is not hollow. No other estate has been swept.

**What is owed:** run that census across the fleet, read-only, and report the estates named rather than fixing them -- the same shape as issue 0498's, where a defect closed as one estate's turned out to be nine more. An estate is only bitten where it BOTH carries such a comment AND arms shellcheck; the census finds the first, and the second is a per-estate question.

**Filed by vc on devbin-vc's measurement and at its request**, so the finding outlives the live channel it was reported in.

## A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTANCE OF THE GENERAL FORM, FROM A DIFFERENT TOOL, THE SAME MORNING (devbin-vc, 2026-09-22)

The paragraph above says a tool whose configuration surface accepts prose will read a comment as configuration, and that **being disarmed is not a state it reports**. That sentence acquired a second instance within hours, in a different mechanism entirely, found during the fleet's concurrency audit.

Laksa's workflow carried a `concurrency:` block that was well formed and carried a comment saying it cancels PRs. Its `cancel-in-progress` read `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`. So it cancelled pull requests and **never cancelled a push** -- hv's ruling exactly inverted -- and every audit grepping for `concurrency:` counted it compliant. It surfaced only because devbin-vc asked for a literal `true` rather than for the key's presence.

**Present, plausible, disarmed, and reporting nothing about being disarmed.** The shellcheck case and the Laksa case share no tool, no syntax and no author, and they share that property exactly. The pairing is why this issue is worth keeping open for a population rather than closing on its instance: **a census that asks whether a mechanism is PRESENT cannot see a mechanism that is present and inverted**, and the only census that can is one that asks what the mechanism is set TO.

That generalises the census this issue already owes. For the shellcheck class the question is whether a comment sits in directive position; for the wider class it is, for each armed mechanism in a tree, whether its disabled state is distinguishable from its enabled state by inspection. The second question has no cheap grep and is not being proposed as work here; it is recorded because the two instances establish that the class is real rather than theoretical.

## THE FLEET CENSUS, RUN 2026-09-22 BY vc, AND ITS ANSWER IS NARROW AND UNCOMFORTABLE

**Every git repository under the estate root was censused, read-only, on its working tree.** The grep is this issue's own -- comments in directive position, minus the six real keys -- and every hit was then CLASSIFIED BY DRIVING THE TOOL rather than by reading the line, because a comment only disarms shellcheck where shellcheck can see it. A `#` line in a workflow outside a `run:` body is a YAML comment and is invisible to it.

**THE INSTRUMENT WAS POSITIVE-CONTROLLED BEFORE ANY SILENCE WAS BELIEVED.** actionlint 1.7.12 was driven against a planted workflow carrying `# shellcheck THIS IS NOT A KEY` inside a `run:` block and reported SC1072 and SC1073 at that step. So actionlint's silence on a real workflow is evidence that the comment is not in a shell body, rather than evidence of nothing.

**FOUR HITS, THREE REPOSITORIES, AND ONLY TWO ARE REAL.**

- **Intent, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, two hits** -- YAML comments attached to `uses:` and job keys, outside every `run:` body. actionlint reports nothing for the file. NOT defects.
- **Utilz, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`** -- a YAML comment above the `test-summary` job's `name:`, outside every `run:` body. actionlint reports nothing for the workflow. NOT a defect.
- **Intent, `tests/unit/critic_arming_census.bats:183`** -- REAL, and landed. `# shellcheck -- a code read cannot tell \`refuses\` from \`would refuse\`.` Driven against HEAD's committed bytes in a scratch copy rather than against a dirty worktree: SC1073 and SC1072, in a 260-line file, so roughly seventy lines have gone unchecked since `c5c9cce14b` on 2026-08-27.
- **`_Archive/Intentv2`, `intent/plugins/claude/lib/critic_runner.sh:280`** -- REAL and inert. Same two codes, in a 576-line file, so roughly half of it is unchecked. This is the archived v2 Bash CLI, which is deleted from the live line and runs nowhere. Recorded for completeness and not owed a fix.

**SO NO ESTATE OUTSIDE INTENT IS BITTEN, AND THE ANSWER THE CENSUS ACTUALLY RETURNED IS WORSE THAN A LIST OF ESTATES WOULD HAVE BEEN.** Both live instances are in Intent, and both are in files whose SUBJECT is shellcheck arming. The file with seventy unchecked lines is `critic_arming_census.bats`, whose entire job is to census whether armed rules are enforced.

## AND A THIRD INSTANCE WAS BEING CREATED WHILE THE CENSUS RAN: THE CLASS REPLICATES BY REFACTORING

**This is the mechanism the issue did not carry, and it is the sharpest thing the census produced.** While censusing, `tests/lib/test_helper.bash` was found to carry a line beginning `# shellcheck ` that `git blame` reports as "Not Committed Yet" -- uncommitted work in the shared checkout, being written at that moment by the node fixing issue 0512. Its own text says it was MOVED from `critic_arming_census.bats`, generalising the function past shellcheck. The move carried the prose across and produced a second instance from the first.

**THE DEFECT PROPAGATES THROUGH ORDINARY, CORRECT REFACTORING**, because prose travels with the code it explains and nothing in a move inspects the prose. A census finds instances; it does not find the copying. And the copy was being made inside the fix for 0512, an issue about instruments that pass without measuring -- so the class was invisible to the node thinking hardest about that exact class, in the exact file where it was thinking about it.

**WHAT THAT ADDS TO THE CENSUS AS A METHOD.** A one-time sweep answers for a moment and cannot answer for the next refactor. The durable form is a check that runs -- and the cheap one already exists, since driving shellcheck or actionlint over a tree finds every instance without a grep and without a key list to keep current. The two live instances above were both found by the grep and CONFIRMED by the tool; the tool alone would have found them both.

**STATUS OF THE TWO LIVE INSTANCES:** routed to the node already holding both files for 0512, with the re-enabled findings owed back -- the count of what has been hiding behind the silence in each file is not yet known, and it is the one number this census cannot supply by inspection.

## CORRECTION, SAME DAY, BY ITS AUTHOR: THE MECHANISM ABOVE IS WRONG AND THE TRUE ONE IS WORSE

**"THE CLASS REPLICATES BY REFACTORING" IS WITHDRAWN.** It is stated above and in the commit that recorded this census, and it is FALSE. It is corrected forward rather than rewritten, per the estate's standing rule on a false claim in a landed commit.

**WHAT WAS INFERRED AND WHAT WAS MEASURED.** The helper's comment says the FUNCTION was moved from `critic_arming_census.bats`, and from that this issue concluded that the PROSE was carried across with it. The two sentences were never compared. Driven afterwards, at the author's own prompting: `critic_arming_census.bats:183` reads `# shellcheck -- a code read cannot tell \`refuses\` from \`would refuse\`` and the helper's read `# shellcheck was cheaper than writing a second one`. They share the first two words and nothing else. Nothing was carried, and the two were written by different hands on different days.

**SO IT IS INDEPENDENT RE-INVENTION, TWICE, IN THE TWO FILES WHOSE SUBJECT IS THE TOOL** -- because that is where the tool's name is likeliest to begin a sentence. **That is the harder finding to defend against.** A refactor is traceable: a move can be inspected, and a rule about moves is at least writable. Two authors independently reaching for the same word at the start of a comment is neither. It also predicts where the next instance will be, which the refactoring story does not: wherever someone is writing carefully ABOUT shellcheck.

## AND THE SEVERITY RAN THE OTHER WAY ROUND FROM THE FRAMING

**NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY SHELLCHECKS A `.bats` FILE**, driven with a positive control on the same bytes two ways: an unquoted expansion in a file named `.bash` yields `[CRITICAL] IN-SH-CODE-001`, and the identical content in a file named `.bats` yields `ok: no shell findings`. The CI job's selector matches no `.bats`, and IN-SH-CODE-001's `applies_to` is `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh` and `bin/*`.

So the landed instance in `critic_arming_census.bats` was **LATENT**: real, worth fixing, and invisible to the gate because the file was never in the gate's population. It truncates shellcheck for a human running it by hand, which is exactly how this census found it. The helper instance, in a `.bash` file, was the **LIVE** one.

**THAT DISTINCTION IS WHAT A HIT IN THIS CENSUS MEANS, and it should be read into every row above.** A hit in a file nothing checks is a trap for a human. A hit in a checked file is a hole in the gate. The census reports both and they are not the same finding.

## WHAT THE SILENCE WAS HIDING, MEASURED FIRST-HAND RATHER THAN ARGUED

The count this census could not supply by inspection came back from the node that fixed the live instance, and it is the strongest evidence this issue has:

**BEFORE the reword, shellcheck on the helper reported SC1073 and SC1072 AND NOTHING ELSE. AFTER it, SC2034 twice, SC2154 twice, SC2016 twice, and SC2086 -- IN-SH-CODE-001, CRITICAL, GATE-BLOCKING -- in the same file, in the same edit.** `intent critic shell` confirmed it: CRITICAL before a sanctioned `disable=SC2086` directive carrying its reason, clean after. The silence was concealing a finding that would have refused that node's own commit.

`critic_arming_census.bats` with its checks re-enabled comes back completely clean, rc 0, no output -- the same result devbin got on its own instance, and worth recording either way.

**THE DURABLE FORM FOLLOWS FROM THE CORRECTED MECHANISM.** Against replication-by-refactor a rule about moves might have sufficed. Against independent re-invention nothing but a running check does, and the check already exists: driving shellcheck or actionlint over a tree finds every instance without a grep and without a key list to keep current.

## RESOLVED 2026-09-22 -- the census is run, both live instances are fixed, and the tools were driven on HEAD rather than the grep re-read

**BOTH REAL INSTANCES ARE GONE, CONFIRMED BY DRIVING THE CHECKER AND NOT BY THE ABSENCE OF A GREP HIT.** At HEAD, `shellcheck` over `tests/lib/test_helper.bash` and over `tests/unit/critic_arming_census.bats` reports SC1072 and SC1073 **zero times** in each. Both were fixed by ic inside 0512's landing, which is where the files were already open.

**THE TWO REMAINING GREP HITS ARE NOT DEFECTS AND THE DISTINCTION IS DRIVEN.** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` carries two comments beginning `# shellcheck ` that sit outside every `run:` body, so they are YAML comments and shellcheck never sees them. `actionlint` reports nothing for that file or for `rust.yml` -- including over the fifty-six lines ic added to it today -- and the instrument was positive-controlled first, against a planted directive-position comment inside a `run:` block, where it fires SC1072 and SC1073. So the silence is evidence rather than an absence of one.

**WHAT THE CENSUS ANSWERED:** no estate outside Intent is bitten. Four hits across three repositories of every git repository under the estate root, of which two were real, one was inert (the archived v2 tree, which runs nowhere) and one was a YAML comment.

**WHAT CLOSING THIS DOES NOT CLAIM.** It does not claim the class cannot recur -- the corrected mechanism is independent re-invention rather than replication, so nothing here prevents the next author beginning a sentence with the tool's name. The durable answer is the one already stated: driving shellcheck or actionlint over a tree finds every instance without a grep and without a key list to keep current, and both live instances were found by the grep and CONFIRMED by the tool. It also does not reach the wider question this issue records and does not propose as work: for each armed mechanism in a tree, whether its disabled state is distinguishable from its enabled state by inspection.
